title: Freeze the cyclist
brief: Photograph the passing cyclist so rider and wheels look completely still, without an underexposed image.
hint: How far does the rider travel in the time the shutter is open? Light has to come from somewhere else if the shutter is short.

title: Show the speed
brief: Make a photo where the cyclist is clearly blurred by motion while the park around them stays crisp.
hint: The camera must stay still while the subject keeps moving.

title: Pan with the cyclist
brief: Keep the rider reasonably sharp while the background streaks behind them.
hint: Follow the rider with the camera and keep swinging through the exposure. A slower shutter makes longer streaks — and makes matching the rider's speed harder.

title: Portrait with separation
brief: A head-and-shoulders portrait where the eyes are sharp and the background melts into soft blur.
hint: Background blur grows with the aperture's physical size and the subject's magnification. Where you stand matters as much as the lens.

title: Sharp from front to back
brief: Crouch by the flowers and make an image that is acceptably sharp from the meadow 2 m in front of you all the way to the distant trees.
hint: Look up the hyperfocal distance — and remember a tiny aperture needs light from somewhere.

title: Freeze a gull's wings
brief: Catch one of the circling gulls large enough to see, with its wing beat frozen and the bird in focus.
hint: Birds are small and far away; wings move much faster than the body.

title: Protect the highlights
brief: Photograph the white pavilion in full sun with detail kept in its brightest walls, and without letting the scene fall into darkness.
hint: Watch the zebras and the right edge of the histogram.
